note: Baseline for the whole-tree security sweep (Issue #4193). Run `deno task security-tree-sweep` from worker/deno (or `deno run --allow-read --allow-write --allow-run --allow-env worker/deno/mod.ts security-tree-sweep --slug stSoftwareAU/VibeCoder` from the repository root). Every deduplicated finding the sweep reports must either be fixed or appear in exactly one list here. `falsePositives` entries need a `reason` explaining why the match is benign. `accepted` entries are real but tolerated risks: they need a `reason` and should carry the tracking `issue` number. Entries match on `path` plus `rule` (a rule family such as `command-injection`, or a tool-native rule id) and, optionally, a `line` anchor within the sweep's 10-line window. The sweep exits non-zero while any finding is unlisted; a stale entry (matching nothing) is reported so it can be removed.

Global replace of `<!--`/`-->` with tokens (`<!- -`, `- ->`) that cannot re-form the pattern with their neighbours; the result is a comment-safe excerpt, and the check that matters is `assert(!out.includes("-->"))` in the tests (Issue #4409 CodeQL triage).
Global replace of `<!--`/`-->` with `<!- -`/`- ->` — replacements that cannot re-form the token; the excerpt is bounded and fenced (Issue #4409 CodeQL triage).

The comment strip only decides whether a body has visible text; the worst case for an unusual comment form is treating a comment-only body as visible, which is the safe direction (Issue #4409 CodeQL triage).

Detection heuristics for LLM API hosts in scanned code (both host patterns in this window): an unanchored host pattern over-matches (`api.anthropic.com.evil`), and over-matching is the safe direction for a detector that only flags for review (Issue #4409 CodeQL js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor).

The pattern requires `/` immediately after `github.com`, so a look-alike host (`github.com.evil/`) does not match; the extracted URLs are then validated against the repository slug downstream (Issue #4409 CodeQL js/regex/missing-regexp-anchor).

The canary is a detection marker planted for one harness run, not key material: a slight modulo bias in its characters does not weaken what it proves (whether the literal reaches an outbound artefact) (Issue #4409 CodeQL js/biased-cryptographic-random).

The pattern comes from the operator's private identifiers file, and a plain literal is metacharacter-escaped before compilation; a `/regex/` entry is the operator's own expression (Issue #4409 semgrep detect-non-literal-regexp).

`applyRename` compiles the operator's own rename rule, and `rule.from` is metacharacter-escaped with `escapeRegExp` immediately above the `new RegExp`, so no pattern syntax reaches the compiler (semgrep detect-non-literal-regexp; same triage as `export_scrub_gate.ts`).

The pattern is a GitHub allow-list glob whose only wildcard is `*`; every other character is escaped before compilation and the glob comes from the repository's own settings (Issue #4409 semgrep detect-non-literal-regexp).

accepted.reason: The `minimumReleaseAge: "0"` the rule flags is the documented first-party exemption for stSoftwareAU/* packages only (Issue #2124); every third-party ecosystem keeps the 24 hours set at the top of the file. Not the emergency override path (docs/security-advisory-triage.md).

`held` is provably true here — the acquire loop only `break`s after setting it and every other exit throws — so the rule is correct. Kept deliberately: the release path states the invariant it depends on, and a future exit added to that loop would make the guard load-bearing. A code-quality observation, not a security finding (js/trivial-conditional).

`timedOut`/`runFinished` are closure flags set from timer and completion callbacks, so the re-check before arming the next watchdog is not redundant at runtime even where the analyser proves it constant along one path. A code-quality observation, not a security finding (js/trivial-conditional).

Same guard as line 1413, on the wind-down path: the flags are mutated by async callbacks between the two checks, which is the reason both exist. A code-quality observation, not a security finding (js/trivial-conditional).
